name: reconciling-medications
description: Drafts a medication reconciliation worksheet and prescriber discrepancy list across care settings: admission, external transfer in or out, discharge hand-off, and outpatient or ED encounters. Builds a best possible medication history (BPMH) from two or more sources (interview, bottles, fill history, outside MAR) and compares it with orders, the discharge list and summary. Flags single-source lists, fill data taken as proof of use, omitted OTC drugs, supplements, inhalers, patches and PRN drugs, dose, route and frequency mismatches, duplication after formulary substitution, holds not resumed, renal dose cuts not revisited, the patient's own supply, allergy conflicts, list versus summary conflicts, look-alike/sound-alike names, and high-alert anticoagulants, insulin and opioids. Applies NPG.14.05.01 (hospitals, 2026; NPSG.03.06.01 elsewhere), WHO High 5s, AHRQ MATCH and 42 CFR 482.43(b). In-stay order continuity goes to reconciling-inpatient-medications. Draft for prescriber review; writes no orders.
